opportunity: kuna's built-in libc prototype table has 27 entries -- a documented minimal stand-in for the Ghidra .gdt archives kuna cannot vendor. Every libc callee outside those 27 leaves its callers' arguments an inferred `unsigned long`. Of the 1587 cases where IDA scores a perfect C type_match and kuna does not, 568 (35.8%) sit in a function that calls a libc name the table did not know, against 395 (24.9%) that call one it did. type_match is kuna's weakest metric on plain C.
test_name: kuna-console verify_libcsigs (5 two-pass e2e assertions on the vendored fauxware fixture) + 5 hermetic table-invariant unit tests
inspiration: Ghidra ApplyDataArchiveAnalyzer (.gdt library archives); IDA Pro's til type libraries
selection_rule: >= 100 call sites over the 547 frozen-decbench C binaries that carry a scored case, OR >= 3 of the 1587 ida-perfect/kuna-imperfect type_match cases, plus a named-witness set (canonicalize_file_name, dirname, asprintf, the err/warn family)

signature_provenance.gcc_aux_info: 193 entries reduced by a fixed rule from the 1520 NC-line prototypes `gcc -aux-info` emits over a TU including the platform headers with _GNU_SOURCE + _FORTIFY_SOURCE=2
signature_provenance.header_redirect: __isoc99_{scanf,sscanf,fscanf} -- /usr/include/stdio.h:434-441 declares them via __REDIRECT FROM scanf/sscanf/fscanf, which is the header proving ABI identity
signature_provenance.gcc_builtin_types: the FORTIFY mem/str _chk family (no header prototype exists -- they are GCC builtins) -- 9 _Static_assert(__builtin_types_compatible_p(...)) checks against GCC's builtin table, all compiling
signature_provenance.hand_spot_check: 16 signatures re-read against their man(3) pages (error, gettext, dcgettext, strsep, getopt_long, mbrtowc, setsockopt, ioctl, getline, reallocarray, strtoul, nl_langinfo, openlog, syslog, strerror, strdup) -- all matched the mechanically derived model

rejected_rather_than_approximated.rule: every modelled slot must be void, exactly 4 bytes, or exactly pointer-width on every ILP32/LP64 target
rejected_rather_than_approximated.note: strtoll is the one that mattered: an earlier reducer classified `long long int` as 4 bytes and would have shipped `int strtoll(...)`. Caught by the width rule, not by review.

wrongness_axis.rule: an entry applies ONLY to a name the image IMPORTS and does not itself define
wrongness_axis.why: zlib's minigzip DEFINES `void error(const char *msg)`; glibc's is `void error(int,int,const char*,...)`. Typing that call error(0,0,...) is strictly worse than the unsigned long it replaces.
wrongness_axis.measured_collision_surface: readelf over all 677 binaries in the frozen O0/O2/O2-noinline trees: the only non-NuttX definition of a new-table name is zlib minigzip's `error` (18 defs / 9 binaries). NuttX implements the genuine POSIX API, so its definitions would have been right anyway -- and the guard makes the statically linked nuttx image byte-identical (0 of 924 functions changed).
wrongness_axis.argument_count_moved_away_note: all 4 sit in two functions (gzip-O2 sub_f900, coreutils-ls-O2ni sub_a550) that ALREADY render free(v43,v24[-8]), malloc(v10,v24[-8]), memcpy(...,v24[-8]) and strlen(v10,v4) -- BASE-table names with 1 parameter -- with this option OFF. A pre-existing frame-recovery defect in those functions, not one this table introduces.
wrongness_axis.parameter_slots_lost_note: both are grep-O2ni Pexecute, `char *` -> `void *`, where the loss is the TRUTHFUL prototype: memchr/rawmemchr really do declare `const void *`.

sweep.surface: kuna decompile-all off vs on, 11 stripped binaries / 5,589 functions, every changed function classified
sweep.binaries: coreutils dircolors (O0), coreutils sort (O2), coreutils ls (O2-noinline), grep (O0), grep (O2-noinline), gzip (O2), zlib minigzip (O0), openssh scp (O0), nuttx (O0, statically linked), leveldb leveldbutil + libleveldb.so (O0, C++)
sweep.structural: gotos essentially flat; no-return annotations identical on every C binary (coreutils-sort abort 24->24 / exit 5->5 / __assert_fail 3->3, grep 28/7/8, openssh-scp error 10->10 exit 39->39); one C++ annotation lost (leveldb sub_77875's __assert_fail) with the emitted control flow unchanged; statically linked nuttx byte-identical.

benchmark.corpus: frozen decbench C corpus (results/full_run), all three optimisation levels, scored with decbench origin/main @325046f, DECBENCH_NO_CACHE=1
benchmark.note: dash carries no DWARF ground truth in the frozen tree, so it scores no functions. coreutils (327 binaries x 2 arms) was started and stopped -- at roughly a minute per whole-binary decompile it is an ~11h run on a box shared with concurrent agents. The five projects above are the measured delta.

speed.decompile: scripts.pipeline.timeit --option libcsigs, grep/main, 15 samples: 1547.61 -> 1547.82 ms (+0.01%), budget 5%
speed.load: interleaved `kuna functions` (load + the whole analysis pass list + commit, no function body decompiled), min AND median of 21 pairs: coreutils-dircolors 293.6 -> 289.4 min (-1.45%) / 321.6 -> 320.7 median (-0.28%); openssh-scp 836.5 -> 835.4 (-0.12%) / 851.9 -> 846.0 (-0.69%); nuttx 1423.4 -> 1432.2 (+0.62%) / 1465.9 -> 1452.2 (-0.93%); grep 849.9 -> 695.4 (-18.18%) / 1012.6 -> 1014.9 (+0.23%) -- the grep MINIMUM is noise in both directions (an earlier 15-pair run of the same case reported +13.99%), the medians are the honest read

notes: No tests/stages/*.xml case: the XML datatest bootstrap builds its program from a <binaryimage> element and never runs the analyzer tier, the same reason verify_cppsig / verify_cppproto / verify_fdeinterior exist. VARIADIC_SUBSTRINGS is deliberately NOT touched -- formatstring/apply.rs matches by `contains`, so __printf_chk is already treated as a format-string callee with the format at slot 0 when it is at slot 1; that is a separate, pre-existing behaviour change and belongs in its own PR.
